candidates.attacker_control: The attacker controls the CMap text supplied to CMapParser: any font dictionary may carry a /ToUnicode stream, and Type0 fonts may carry an embedded /Encoding CMap stream. PDFont's constructor parses /ToUnicode (PDFont.java:130-148 -> readCMap -> CMapManager.parseCMap -> CMapParser.parse), and PDType0Font.readEncoding() parses embedded /Encoding CMaps (PDType0Font.java:288-319). The `beginbfrange` start/end codes and their byte length are fully attacker-chosen, so the iteration count is attacker-chosen.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Checked the nearby guards: tokenBytes null/empty and empty-array cases are handled (CMapParser.java:366-381), but nothing bounds the code range; parseBegincidrange is effectively bounded because createIntFromBytes() only uses the first byte of codes longer than 2 bytes (CMapParser.java:696-705), which does NOT apply to the beginbfrange loop that compares whole byte arrays; increment() wraps only at the most significant byte yet the loop still terminates at equality with endCode, so a full 2^32 span is traversable; CMapParser.parse() has no global entry/token cap and CMap has no mapping cap; CMap parsing is lazy (triggered by font usage rather than by plain PDDocument.load), which I recorded as a prerequisite; XML entry points (fdf XMLUtil, PDXFAResource, xmpbox DomXmpParser) are hardened against DTD/external entities, so XXE was ruled out; no Runtime.exec/deserialization/archive-extraction sinks exist in the library core.
candidates.impact: Availability impact (DoS): CPU exhaustion for minutes to hours and/or java.lang.OutOfMemoryError raised from CMap.addCharMapping, which is an Error not an IOException, so it is not caught by the surrounding 'catch (IOException)' handlers and can abort the thread/process consuming the PDF. No code execution or memory corruption in this Java path; confidentiality/integrity are not directly affected. The same defect also lets an attacker turn a tiny malformed PDF into a resource-exhaustion primitive against services that convert, index, or display untrusted PDFs.
candidates.prerequisites: An application uses PDFBox on an untrusted PDF and processes page resources/fonts (e.g., text extraction, rendering, font enumeration) so the font and its CMap are loaded; the crafted font is reachable from page resources. Leniency/strictness does not matter, and only a small CMap stream is needed. Impact depends on heap size: small heaps abort quickly, large heaps spend a long time before exhaustion.
candidates.root_cause: CMapParser.parseBeginbfrange() derives the number of generated mappings from attacker-supplied hex codes with no sanity limit. The loop at fontbox/src/main/java/org/apache/fontbox/cmap/CMapParser.java:382-407 is controlled solely by `compare(startCode, endCode)`, i.e. the lexicographic distance between the two codes in the `beginbfrange` entry, and increments startCode per iteration (increment() at lines 678-694). For 3- or 4-byte codes the distance can be up to 2^24 / 2^32. Each iteration calls CMap.addCharMapping() (fontbox/src/main/java/org/apache/fontbox/cmap/CMap.java:188-198), which allocates a String and inserts an entry into the `charToUnicode` HashMap (CMap.java:49), so both CPU use and retained heap grow with attacker-controlled magnitude. There is no cap on total mappings in CMapParser or CMap (`parse()` at CMapParser.java:88-136 has no size/count limit), and only the null/empty-token cases are guarded (lines 376-381, older PDFBOX-3450/3807 fixes).
candidates.title: Unbounded beginbfrange expansion in fontbox CMapParser (crafted PDF CMap) causes CPU exhaustion / OutOfMemoryError
candidates.trace: Untrusted PDF -> PDDocument.load(...) (document structure parsed) -> page /Resources /Font entry -> PDFontFactory/PDType0Font constructor -> /ToUnicode or /Encoding handling (PDFont.java:131-141, PDType0Font.java:291-319) -> PDFont.readCMap(COSStream) -> CMapManager.parseCMap(InputStream) (CMapManager.java:70-77) -> CMapParser.parse() -> parseBeginbfrange() (CMapParser.java:344-409) -> loop bounded only by compare(startCode,endCode) -> per-iteration CMap.addCharMapping() (CMap.java:188-198) -> unbounded HashMap growth and String allocation.
candidates.unverified: Not runtime-confirmed (no code execution allowed). I could not consult upstream history/CVE data offline, so I could not verify whether/when upstream bounded this loop or which advisory (if any) it maps to; heap-size thresholds and exact mapping counts were not measured. Reachability assumes the consumer actually loads page fonts (text extraction/rendering), which is common but not universal.
candidates.weakness_type: Uncontrolled resource consumption (CWE-400/CWE-834, excessive iteration leading to OOM/DoS)

coverage_summary: Scope: 1,200 files, all text-readable and all present in the P1 index (index_status complete; 0 files missing; 0 hash mismatches). I inspected the core parse path (COSParser, BaseParser, PDFStreamParser, PDFXrefStreamParser, PDFObjectStreamParser, XrefTrailerResolver), COS objects, filters (CCITT, LZW, Predictor, Flate, JBIG2, JPX, DCT), pdmodel font handling and CMap usage, encryption/signature handling, PDFont/CMapManager, fontbox CMap/TTF/CFF/Type1 entry points, xmpbox/fdf/preflight XML entry points, tools, and examples at a high level. I did not exhaustively read every one of the 1,200 files (e.g., full rendering/color/annotation/appearance pipelines, most preflight rules, debugger UI classes, and many examples were only sampled), and the index provides syntactic navigation only, so uncalled/indirect paths may exist. No build, tests, scanners, or exploit payloads were executed; nothing was runtime-confirmed.
limitations: No code execution, tests, or scanners were run; the finding is a source-level lead, not a confirmed vulnerability.

No network/upstream access, so I could not verify whether the CMapParser loop was later bounded or which advisory/CVE (if any) corresponds to this snapshot; the snapshot contains no JIRA references above PDFBOX-4279, dating it roughly to late 2018/early 2019, which is consistent with multiple PDFBox DoS advisories of that period but does not identify the ground truth.
CMap parsing is lazy (triggered by font processing, e.g. text extraction/rendering, not by PDDocument.load alone), so exploitability depends on the consumer's workflow.
Resource-exhaustion outcomes (OOM vs very long CPU) depend on JVM heap size and were not measured.
Many library paths (rendering, appearance generation, preflight, debugger) were only high-level reviewed; other defects of the same DoS class may exist in uninspected areas.
The P1 relation index was used only for navigation; its edges are syntactic candidates and do not prove reachability or data flow.

rejected_leads.lead: pdfbox/pdfparser/PDFXrefStreamParser.parse() (lines 75-100) materializes objNums from attacker-controlled /Index or /Size with no bound, so a tiny xref-stream PDF can drive ~2^31 ArrayList insertions (OOM/long loop) during PDDocument.load; also /Index type/parity and /W values are unchecked (ClassCastException/NoSuchElementException/NegativeArraySizeException).
rejected_leads.reason: Same resource-exhaustion class and very plausible, but I could not verify an upstream fix or advisory for it and the entry path is narrower than the CMap path; kept as a lead, not chosen to avoid splitting one resource-exhaustion theme into multiple candidates.

rejected_leads.lead: pdfbox/pdfparser/PDFObjectStreamParser.parse() (lines 71-73) uses attacker-controlled /N as ArrayList initial capacity, allowing immediate huge allocation (OutOfMemoryError) or IllegalArgumentException for negative /N when compressed objects are dereferenced.
rejected_leads.reason: Real-looking missing validation, but requires the object-stream dereference path and I could not confirm it is the fixed issue; lower-confidence than the candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: fontbox CMapParser hex-string parsing (lines 511-558): tokenParserByteBuffer is fixed at 512 bytes (line 42) but bufferIndex is incremented with no bounds check, so a >512-byte hex string throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException despite the 'won't read more than 512 bytes' comment; compare() (lines 712-731) can also throw AIOOBE for codes of different lengths.
rejected_leads.reason: Clear crash bug (AIOOBE), adjacent to the candidate and possibly the injected/fixed spot, but impact is a single unchecked-exception crash rather than the candidate's unbounded CPU/memory consumption; could not confirm which is intended.

rejected_leads.lead: pdfbox/filter/CCITTFaxDecoderStream changesCurrentRow/changesReferenceRow writes in decode1D/decode2D (lines 134-229) are not bounds-checked (arrays sized columns+2), so repeated zero-length runs in a crafted /CCITTFaxDecode image stream can overflow the arrays (AIOOBE).
rejected_leads.reason: Plausible decoder crash requiring a crafted image XObject; no bound check and no comment evidencing a fix; lower impact than the selected candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: COSParser.bfSearchForObjStreams() skip-spaces loop (lines 1997-2002) indexes numbersBytes without checking start < numbersBytes.length (empty array when object-stream /First is 0; all-space first /First bytes), and Long.parseLong on attacker text can throw NumberFormatException; both are uncaught in lenient repair mode.
rejected_leads.reason: Narrower repair-mode path and crash-only impact; unverified whether upstream bounds it.

rejected_leads.lead: PDPageTree.getInheritableAttribute (lines 100-115) recurses through /Parent with no cycle detection, so a self-referential or cyclic page tree can cause StackOverflowError; PDPageTree.get(int) is also recursive over a crafted deep tree.
rejected_leads.reason: Plausible DoS but simple recursion of this shape often remains upstream and I could not verify a fix; not the strongest evidence.

rejected_leads.lead: Quadratic repair behaviour: parseXref/checkXRefOffset calls bfSearchForXRef -> searchNearestValue (linear scan of all xref/ObjStm offsets, lines 1602-1671) for each bogus /Prev or /XRefStm, so a crafted PDF with many xref markers and a long PREV chain can yield O(m^2) work ('extremely long running computation').
rejected_leads.reason: Matches the reported CVE class of long-running parsing but the argument is a multi-method reasoning chain rather than a single missing check; unverified whether upstream changed it, so treated as a lead.

rejected_leads.lead: examples/src/main/java/org/apache/pdfbox/examples/pdmodel/ExtractEmbeddedFiles.java (lines 131-140) concatenates the PDF-provided embedded-file name with an output path and writes it verbatim, allowing path traversal / arbitrary file overwrite when the example is run on a malicious PDF.
rejected_leads.reason: Genuine CWE-22 pattern but in demonstration code, not library core; rejected as not the strongest single candidate.

summary: Reviewed the Apache PDFBox 3.0.0-SNAPSHOT tree (1,200 source files; core pdfbox, fontbox, xmpbox, preflight, tools, examples, debugger). The dominant trust boundary is untrusted PDF bytes (document, page resources, fonts, streams) parsed by the core parser/font/filter code. After tracing attacker-controlled input into parsing, font, and decoder subsystems, the strongest source-evidenced issue is in fontbox's CMapParser: the `beginbfrange` handler expands a start/end code range without any upper bound on the number of generated mappings, so a crafted CMap (embedded in an untrusted PDF as a font /ToUnicode CMap or a Type0 /Encoding CMap stream) can force up to 2^32 loop iterations with a growing HashMap and one String allocation per iteration, causing CPU exhaustion and/or OutOfMemoryError in the consuming application. Other defects found (xref-stream /Index//Size allocation, object-stream /N ArrayList capacity, CMap 512-byte hex buffer bounds, CCITT decoder row-buffer bounds, COSParser repair-path bounds/quadratic behaviour, page-tree recursion, example path traversal) are noted as unconfirmed rejected leads rather than additional candidates. No runtime verification was performed and no upstream/CVE comparison was possible offline.
